title: Terraform VPC Modules (Alpha) — Release Checklist
content:
Context
- This checklist is for cutting alpha releases of the AWS Private VPC Terraform module suite in `redwood-terraform`.
- Goal: predictable, reproducible releases with clear compatibility, safety notes, and a tight loop with design partner pilots.
- Alpha rule of thumb: prefer a “safe default + documented extension point” over adding knobs. If we must add knobs, document supported combinations and what we’ll support in pilot.

Scope (what this checklist covers)
- Version bump + tag + GitHub release
- CHANGELOG + release notes
- CI green (fmt/validate/tflint/checkov + unit-ish module tests)
- Integration tests (ephemeral VPC) status + gating decision
- Docs updates (Confluence + docs site quickstart where applicable)
- Pilot comms (design partners + internal support readiness)

Owners / required sign-offs (alpha)
- Release driver (this run): Release Eng (Connor O'Brien / Devon Price)
- Infra owner approval: Irene Choi
- Security approval when security-sensitive diffs exist (IAM/logging/endpoints/egress): Marcus Lin or Naomi Feldman (PM) + Security Eng delegate
- Docs approval when public/internal docs change: Elliot Price or Kira Thompson
- Field readiness confirmation for pilot-impacting changes: Markus Klein (SE)

Pre-flight (do before you touch versions)
[ ] Confirm the target release train
    - Patch (x.y.Z): non-breaking bugfixes, doc fixes, defaults that do not change behavior for existing users
    - Minor (x.Y.0): additive features, new modules, new outputs, additional endpoints, optional flags defaulting to existing behavior
    - Major (X.0.0): breaking changes (avoid during alpha unless explicitly approved via PM-928 process)

[ ] Confirm what’s included in the release (write down the PR list)
    - Use merged PRs since last tag.
    - Make sure each PR has:
      - Clear description, risk notes, and any required migration steps
      - “Alpha constraints” callouts if the change reduces supported topologies

[ ] Identify any customer-impacting behavior change
    - Examples:
      - NAT gateway count/placement assumptions
      - Endpoint private DNS defaults
      - Route table changes
      - Changes to VPC Flow Logs destination/retention semantics
      - Security group egress tightening (common cause of “installer can’t pull images”)

[ ] Validate compatibility commitments (alpha)
    - Terraform version pin: confirm matches repo standard
    - AWS provider version pin: confirm matches CI
    - Supported regions/AZ assumptions: call out explicitly (esp. anything with 2-AZ vs 3-AZ behavior)

Versioning + tagging
[ ] Determine new version
    - Follow semver as defined in the module versioning standard.
    - Alpha note: if the change is “breaking for some” due to constraints, treat as breaking and either:
      (a) keep default behavior and gate new behavior behind an opt-in variable, or
      (b) bump major and update pilot plan + support readiness.

[ ] Update versions consistently
    - Root module versions (if pinned in examples)
    - Example environments (tfvars / example stacks)
    - Any release workflow metadata files

[ ] Create release branch (if required by current repo policy)
    - `release/vX.Y.Z`
    - Keep release branch minimal: version bump + changelog + release notes only.

Changelog + release notes (must be done before tagging)
[ ] Update CHANGELOG
    - Add entry for vX.Y.Z with date.
    - Format:
      - Added / Changed / Fixed / Security / Known Issues
      - “Migration notes” section for anything that could alter deployed resources

[ ] Add/Update Alpha Release Notes page (Confluence + docs site if applicable)
    - Include:
      - Modules included in this release
      - Notable changes and whether they are opt-in
      - Known limitations
      - Support / escalation guidance (Slack channel + ticket path)
      - Explicit callout: “Alpha – pin versions; avoid auto-upgrade”

[ ] Write “What changed for pilots?” paragraph
    - 5–10 lines aimed at Solutions Eng + customer platform engineers.
    - Include expected impact, any action required, and “if you see X error, check Y” hints.

CI / quality gates
[ ] Ensure CI is green on the release commit
    - terraform fmt
    - terraform validate
    - tflint
    - checkov (or equivalent)
    - provider version pin checks

[ ] Security scanning results reviewed
    - If checkov suppressions were added/changed:
      - Confirm suppression is justified and documented
      - Confirm Security sign-off (Marcus Lin delegate) if it changes risk posture

[ ] Integration tests status recorded
    - Ephemeral VPC integration tests can be:
      - Required per-release, or
      - Allowed to run nightly with a “last known good” requirement

    Release rule (alpha):
    - If infra behavior changes (routing, endpoints, NAT, IAM, flow logs), integration tests must have a green run within the last 72 hours OR run on-demand before tagging.
    - If docs-only + metadata changes, nightly green is acceptable.

[ ] Manual smoke plan (if tests are skipped)
    - Record who accepted the risk (Infra lead) and where (link to Slack thread or Linear comment).

Documentation checklist
[ ] Confluence deployment guide updated if any step changes
    - Prereqs
    - Minimal inputs
    - Validation steps
    - Handoff to installer steps

[ ] Quickstart template updated (if examples changed)
    - Ensure minimal variable set still works.
    - Ensure example tfvars do not contain customer-specific sensitive info.

[ ] Installer compatibility check
    - If endpoints/DNS/IAM outputs changed, confirm installer docs / preflight checks remain accurate.
    - If needed, coordinate follow-up PR to installer docs or preflight logic.

[ ] “Supported topologies and extension points” section still accurate
    - Especially around:
      - Private EKS control plane assumptions
      - Endpoint private DNS behavior
      - VPN/DX placeholders and what we do NOT configure

Release execution (tag + publish)
[ ] Merge release PR
    - Required approvals collected (see sign-offs section).

[ ] Tag the release
    - Create annotated git tag `vX.Y.Z` on the merge commit.

[ ] Create GitHub Release
    - Title: `vX.Y.Z (alpha)`
    - Paste CHANGELOG entry.
    - Attach any generated artifacts if the workflow produces them.

[ ] Verify module source references in docs/examples
    - Ensure examples reference the new tag.
    - Ensure no examples point to `main`.

Pilot comms + support readiness
[ ] Notify design partners (email + Slack)
    - Audience: Acme Bank pilot, Northstar Healthcare pilot (if active), plus any new design partners tracked in PM-913.
    - Include:
      - Version number
      - What changed
      - Whether they should upgrade now or wait
      - Upgrade instructions + pinning guidance
      - Known issues + troubleshooting pointers

[ ] Notify internal channels
    - #eng-infra (release complete + link)
    - #eng-private-deployments (what changed + any installer implications)
    - #support (what to watch for; include known failure modes)

[ ] Update pilot plan / weekly check-in notes
    - If the release requires customer action, make it a standing agenda item.

Post-release verification (same day)
[ ] Confirm no immediate regressions reported in Slack/support
[ ] Validate “new tag works” by running:
    - `terraform init` in the quickstart template
    - `terraform plan` with a minimal tfvars

[ ] Capture follow-ups
    - Any “we should document this” goes into docs ticket.
    - Any customer pain discovered goes into requirements matrix / known issues.

Rollback / hotfix guidance (alpha)
- We generally do not delete tags. If a release is bad:
  1) Cut a patch release vX.Y.(Z+1) that reverts or fixes.
  2) Update release notes to explicitly warn against vX.Y.Z.
  3) Notify pilots + support with the mitigation.

Common gotchas (from pilots)
- ECR image pulls failing: missing ECR endpoints and/or private DNS behavior mismatched.
- Intermittent DNS in private subnets: resolver settings + endpoint DNS configuration; validate before installer.
- NAT gateway AZ assumptions: ensure subnet mapping supports the customer’s AZ count.

Notes / placeholders
- Add the release email template link here (TODO: centralize in SE playbook).
- Add “release dashboard” link here once the CI pipeline exposes a stable URL (TODO Devon).
